deep.reconstruction:
Context: on p.45 Grothendieck defines groupoids of topological surfaces with extra structure. Objects are triples (X, Σ̃, R): X a compact oriented surface with boundary, Σ̃ = ∂X ⊔ Σ a family of disjoint circles (Σ being the 'cercles de découpage', the cut circles), and R ⊂ Σ̃ a finite set of rigidification points. Arrows are isotopy classes of orientation-preserving homeomorphisms. His announced goal is to determine π0 of the decomposition groupoid S_*TD_top. This page introduces the combinatorial invariant used for that.

**The groupoid Grbip.** Its objects, 'graphes bipondérés' (bi-weighted graphs), are written in the half-edge formalism (S, A→, σ, o):
- S and A→ are finite sets.
- σ is an involution of A→.
- o: A→ → S is the 'origin' map.
- Pairs {a, σa} with a ≠ σa are ordinary edges. Loops and multiple edges are allowed, and so are isolated vertices.
- Fixed points of σ are 'arêtes libres' (free edges, open edges). In modern terms these are legs or tails.

The two weightings are:
- γ: S → ℕ, the genus or 'weight' of each vertex.
- A second map with values in ℕ. On this page it is first written on the free edges A_ℓ (with a deleted attempt to weight S̃ = S ⊔ A_ℓ). The margin admits 'I indicated a weighting of the vertices but not of the edges.' On p.47 it is settled as ρ: Ã = A ⊔ A_ℓ → ℕ, C ↦ #(R ∩ C), the number of rigidification points on each circle.

Arrows of Grbip are isomorphisms of such structures (the word read as 'Fluides' is 'Flèches'). An equivalent description: an ordinary graph without legs (σ acting freely on A→_o = A→ \ A→^σ), plus a finite set A_ℓ and a map A_ℓ → S.

Margin bookkeeping:
- A→ = A→_o ⊔ A→_ℓ, with A→_o → A of degree 2 and A→_ℓ → A_ℓ a bijection.
- Ã = A→/σ = A ⊔ A_ℓ.
- The order (valence) of a vertex is σ(s) = σ_ℓ(s) + σ_o(s): legs plus internal half-edges. These correspond respectively to holes (boundary circles) and to the gluing circles.
- The figure shows a genus-labelled graph with loops, multiple edges and legs: a 'stable graph' picture.

**Purpose (p.47).** A functor Γ sends (X, Σ̃, R) to:
- S = π0(X \ Σ̃);
- half-edges = (circle, side);
- σ = exchange of sides, fixed on boundary circles;
- γ = genus of the pieces;
- ρ = #R ∩ C.

It is claimed to induce a bijection on π0 and a surjection on π1, a '0-isomorphism'. This classifies the topological types of surfaces with a cut system and marked points on the circles by such weighted graphs.

Grothendieck labels these 'MD' (Mumford–Deligne) graphs. They are the dual graphs of boundary strata of moduli of stable curves, enriched by a count of marked points per circle.
errors: No stability condition (e.g. 2γ(s)−2+val(s)>0) is imposed. Discs, annuli and similar pieces are allowed, so the graphs are not the strictly 'stable' graphs of Deligne–Mumford theory. This is consistent with his topological setting rather than an error.

The phrase 'boucles fermées' is ambiguous. A vertex-free closed loop cannot be encoded in the (S, A→, σ, o) formalism, since o maps to S. He presumably means loops at a vertex. Such loops do arise: a non-separating cut circle with both sides in the same piece.

The first attempt to define the second weighting (on A_ℓ only, or on S̃ = S ⊔ A_ℓ) is wrong for the intended functor. Rigidification points can lie on interior cut circles too, so the weighting must be on all of Ã = A ⊔ A_ℓ. Grothendieck notices this himself in the margin and corrects it on p.47.
The margin remark that the definition of 'pondération' is not precise enough and should be replaced by something else ('pol. comb.'?) is left unresolved on this page.

ideas.what: Graphs encoded as (half-edges, involution, origin map), with fixed points of the involution as free edges/legs
ideas.modern_name: Half-edge (flag) formalism for graphs with legs, as in modular operads
ideas.usually_credited_to: Kontsevich–Manin (1994), Getzler–Kapranov (Modular operads, 1998). Serre's Trees uses the fixed-point-free version.
ideas.where_published: Closely related permutation encodings of maps appear in Esquisse d'un programme (1984). The legs-as-fixed-points version is not known to me in his published texts.

ideas.what: Genus-weighted graph with legs as dual graph of a surface cut along disjoint circles (named 'MD' = Mumford–Deligne)
ideas.modern_name: Stable graph / dual graph of a boundary stratum of M̄_{g,n}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne–Mumford (1969); systematized by Kontsevich–Manin and Getzler–Kapranov
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the Teichmüller tower and Mumford–Deligne stratification in prose, not this explicit formalism.

ideas.what: Second weighting on edges and legs counting marked points on each circle (ρ(C) = #R∩C), making the graph 'bipondéré'
ideas.modern_name: Decorated stable graphs for surfaces with marked points on boundary/cut circles (close to bordered-surface or open–closed combinatorics)
ideas.usually_credited_to: No single standard attribution; similar decorations appear in work on bordered surfaces and ribbon-graph models (e.g. Penner, Kaufmann–Penner)

ideas.what: Valence decomposition σ(s) = σ_ℓ(s) + σ_o(s) (legs = holes, internal half-edges = gluing circles)
ideas.modern_name: Valence of a vertex in a stable graph

ideas.what: Using the graph functor to compute π0 of the decomposition groupoid (iso on π0, surjective on π1)
ideas.modern_name: Classification of topological types of multicurves / pants decompositions by dual graphs; π0 of the cut-system complex modulo the mapping class group

missed.claim: In 1983 Grothendieck already uses the exact half-edge/legs formalism for genus-labelled graphs (S, A→, σ involution with fixed points = legs, o: A→ → S, γ: S → ℕ). This is essentially the definition of stable graphs later standard in modular-operad theory, and he explicitly ties it to Mumford–Deligne. It is a priority detail not recorded in the literature.
missed.quote: graphes (S,A→,σ,o) ... des "arêtes libres" ... correspondant aux pts fixes de σ ... S →γ ℕ (application "genre" ou "poids")
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is of historical interest for the genealogy of modular operads and stable-graph combinatorics. It shows the formalism arising from Teichmüller groupoid / Lego considerations a decade before Getzler–Kapranov.

missed.claim: The bi-weighting by number of rigidification points on each circle, edges included, makes these graphs index topological types of surfaces with marked points on boundary and cut circles. The marginal hint that the weighting should be replaced by a finer combinatorial object ('pol. comb.') was not pursued here.
missed.quote: pas assez précis comme définition de "pondération" d'un graphe ; il doit être remplacé par celle d'un pol. comb.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This could relate to decorated graph complexes for bordered surfaces and open–closed moduli. However, it is likely subsumed by later work, and its novelty is modest.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a careful definition of genus-weighted graphs with legs in the half-edge formalism, explicitly named after Mumford–Deligne, with an extra edge weighting by marked points. Mathematically it is routine by today's standards. Historically it is a nice anticipation (1983) of the formalism standardized by Kontsevich–Manin and Getzler–Kapranov, but not a new result.
transcription_corrections: 'Fluides' at bottom should read 'Flèches' (arrows): 'Flèches : Les iso. des telles structures'.
'indice de signification' is more plausibly 'indice de rigidification', consistent with R = sommets de rigidification and ρ(C) = Card(R∩C) on p.47.
The second weighting map is labelled r (later ρ). Its domain was first written as A→^σ = A_ℓ, then (p.47) extended to Ã = A ⊔ A_ℓ.
In the first marginal note, 'avec π arêtes [?]' is uncertain. The reading 'pol. comb.' (polyèdre combinatoire?) is tentative.
